turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come on in, Aoife, grab a seat. You look done in. What's brought you along?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm wrecked, if I'm honest. It's the spots mostly, and my periods are all over the place.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Tell me about the spots, in your own time.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Chin and along the jaw. Big sore ones, not the tiny ones. Two years of it now and I'm sick of looking at them.
[SEG0005] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She stands at the mirror for ages covering them before the shop. It's really getting her down.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): I can talk for myself, thanks. It's embarrassing, that's all. Can we just get on with it?
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Of course we can. And the periods, how are they these days?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): They were monthly and grand. Now it's every two or three months if I even get one. Same two years. Um.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any pain with them when they do arrive?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Not really pain. They just don't show up. And I've hair on my chin and a bit on the lip, I pluck it in the car like an eejit.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): When did you first notice that hair?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm. Maybe a year? I don't know exactly. It crept up.
[SEG0013] person_3 (CAREGIVER): And the weight, doctor. Her clothes are after getting very tight.
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah alright. I was going to say two stone, well actually about a stone and a half since last summer. Jeans won't close. I'm wrecked even when I've slept.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): That's a fair bit to deal with on top of work. May I look at your face and feel your tummy?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Go on, so. Your hands are probably cold.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mm. Inflamed spots along the jawline, and coarse dark hairs on the chin and the upper lip. Tummy is soft, no masses. We weighed you on the way in, seventy eight kilos.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): Have you been putting anything on the spots, or taking tablets?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Just that benzoil peroxide wash from the chemist, the five percent. Most nights. Barely touches them, waste of money.
[SEG0020] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Her sister is always on about biotin, the one with the pressures. And my husband takes metformin for his own sugar, but that's nothing to do with Aoife.
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm not swallowing her biotin. Or his tablets. Jesus.
[SEG0022] person_1 (DOCTOR): No, we won't be using anyone else's medicine. Is there sugar or blood pressure or women's troubles in the family?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): My father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, and another sister has pressure but no sugar. The older one is grand as far as I know.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): What about the day to day stuff, work and food and that?

[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): I work in a clothes shop on Grafton Street. Nine till half five, five days, and the odd Saturday, so the hours are long enough. Diet is rotten, I skip breakfast and it's wraps and takeaways most evenings. Exercise I don't, I get the bus, and I drink a few glasses of wine at the weekend, maybe four or five.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any bad reactions to medicines, antibiotics, painkillers, anything at all?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): No, never. I have taken penicillin and everything, the amoxicillin one, no bother.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): And your breathing, your chest, any trouble there?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Chest is fine.

[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right. Putting the sore spots, the periods every few months, the facial hair and the weight together, I'd be thinking of polycystic ovary syndrome. Only a working idea, not a firm diagnosis.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): PCOS. Brilliant. So that's why I'm floored tired as well, is it?
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): It can travel with it, but I won't hang the tiredness on that until we see tests. We'll do bloods, a hormone panel and a check of your sugar, and a pelvic ultrasound.
[SEG0033] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Does she have to fast? She goes woozy if she misses food. Sorry, the bus was a nightmare getting here, we were late.
[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): Fasting bloods, yes, water only from the night before. The pelvic scan doesn't need fasting, and we'll book that through the clinic.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Someone said the pill would sort the periods. Should I just start one?

[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): The combined pill can steady the periods and help the spots, but I'm not starting you on it today. Don't start any pill yourself until we have these results and we talk it through.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Fine. I wasn't mad keen anyway. Your waiting room is freezing, I nearly walked out.
[SEG0038] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll mention the heating, that's not on. Come back and see me in three weeks with the results, whether you're feeling better or not.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Three weeks. If the shop will let me off. Uh, alright.
[SEG0040] person_1 (DOCTOR): We'll work around the shop hours if we can. Mind yourself going home.

spec.situation: Young woman with acne and irregular periods for two years, some facial hair, weight gain; mother had diabetes; bloods and pelvic scan planned; contraceptive pill discussed, not started.

traps.happens: In ONE long answer the patient lists several relatives and their conditions ('my father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, another sister has pressure but no sugar'), and in another long answer their job, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol.
traps.label_rule: Every relative with a stated condition is a separate family_history entry (relative, condition). Relatives said NOT to have a condition are not family_history entries. Occupation, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol/tobacco each become social_history entries as said (no inventions). Nothing from the doctor's questions is a fact.

traps.happens: The doctor asks about drug reactions. Variants (use ONE per encounter): (a) the patient says 'No, never, I have taken penicillin and everything' (no allergy); (b) the patient is unsure ('maybe the antibiotic or the painkiller, nobody told me which'); (c) a real allergy with the reaction described; (d) allergies are never asked.
traps.label_rule: (a) NO allergy entry: negative_findings 'Allergies' absent. (b) allergy with status uncertain, the substance as described, the reaction if said, plus an allergy_uncertain uncertainty. (c) allergy with the reaction. (d) nothing at all. NEVER list a medicine the patient has taken without a reaction as an allergy, and the plan must not prescribe a drug of a recorded allergy's family.

features: third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.
doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).

omissions.text: Weight gain amount was specified as about 1.5 stone since last summer.
Fatigue detail: patient is 'wrecked even when I've slept' / tired despite sleep.
Abdominal examination also found abdomen/tummy soft, not just no masses.
Family history also included mother does not have diabetes and older sister is well/no known diabetes or hypertension.
Allergy history included tolerance of penicillin/amoxicillin without any reaction.
Negative finding recorded incompletely: patient denied chest trouble as well as breathing trouble ('Chest is fine').
Doctor said tiredness could be associated with PCOS but should not be attributed to it until tests are back.
Blood tests were specifically instructed to be fasting, with water only from the night before; pelvic ultrasound does not require fasting and would be booked through the clinic.
Doctor advised that the combined pill can help regulate periods and improve acne, but was not being started today.
